zones.label: Georgian Bay & Northern Boreal
zones.blurb: Killarney's pink granite and Hwy 129's boreal canyon set the tone before the real distances begin.
tips: Top off fuel in Thessalon — services thin out fast heading north on Hwy 129.
Killarney's Herbert Fisheries is worth timing lunch around.
Crown-land pull-offs north of Thessalon are free but arrive with daylight to scout a spot.

safety.cellCoverage: Patchy once off Hwy 400/17 onto Hwy 129 — download offline maps first.
safety.note: Standard 911 coverage on the main highways; gaps on Hwy 129 itself.

pois.name: Petro-Canada Parry Sound
pois.note: Fuel and diesel just off Hwy 400 as you enter Parry Sound heading north.

pois.name: Coniston Esso
pois.note: Esso stop on Hwy 17 E on Sudbury's eastern edge, good last-fuel before Espanola.

pois.name: Espanola Esso (331 Hwy 17 W)
pois.note: Esso/Circle K right on Hwy 17 through Espanola, easy pull-in for gas and snacks.

pois.name: Blind River Esso (498 Causley St)
pois.note: Reliable fuel stop on Hwy 17 in Blind River before heading north on Hwy 129.

pois.name: Thessalon Esso
pois.note: Last major fuel in Thessalon before the long stretch north on Hwy 129.

pois.name: Herbert Fisheries
pois.note: Iconic lakeside fish-and-chips shack in Killarney village, a must-stop road-trip classic.

pois.name: Loretta's Bakery & Marketplace
pois.note: Well-loved bakery/market just south of Parry Sound off Hwy 400, great pies and baked goods to go.

pois.name: French River Trading Post
pois.note: Historic Hwy 69 roadside outpost with restaurant, gifts, and a scenic French River bridge view.

pois.name: The Little Brew Cafe
pois.note: Small-town cafe in Massey for coffee and a bite between Espanola and Blind River.

pois.name: A Touch of Home Bakery
pois.note: Locally loved bakery in Blind River, good for treats before the Hwy 129 push north.

pois.name: George Lake Campground, Killarney Provincial Park
pois.note: Reservable drive-in campground with showers, good base for hiking The Crack, RV-friendly sites.

pois.name: Chutes Provincial Park Campground
pois.note: Riverside campground right in Massey with waterfall trails steps from the sites.

pois.name: Mississagi Provincial Park Campground
pois.note: Remote, quiet park north of Elliot Lake off Hwy 639, good backcountry-feel car camping.

pois.name: Thessalon Lakeside Park Campground
pois.note: In-town campground on Lake Huron shoreline in Thessalon, easy overnight before heading north.

pois.name: Crown Land Camping, Hwy 129 / Mississagi River corridor
pois.note: Free dispersed Crown-land pull-offs along Hwy 129 north of Thessalon, popular with van/RV boondockers.

pois.name: The Crack Trail
pois.note: Killarney's signature strenuous hike to a dramatic quartzite ridge with panoramic views.

pois.name: Chikanishing Trail
pois.note: Easy loop along pink granite Georgian Bay shoreline, great short leg-stretcher stop.

pois.name: Bridal Veil Falls (Kagawong)
pois.note: Popular walk-behind waterfall on Manitoulin Island, worth the short detour from Espanola.

pois.name: Chutes Provincial Park Waterfalls
pois.note: Short riverside trail past cascading falls right off Hwy 17 in Massey, easy scenic stop.

pois.name: Mississagi River Valley Viewpoint (Hwy 129)
pois.note: One of Ontario's most scenic drives, a winding canyon-like valley with pull-off lookouts.

pois.name: Potholes Provincial Nature Reserve
pois.note: Glacial pothole rock formations near Elliot Lake, a quick offbeat nature stop.

zones.label: Lake Superior North Shore
zones.blurb: The most scenic and most remote stretch of the whole route — Hwy 17 hugging the lake through Pukaskwa, Wawa, and Sault Ste. Marie.
tips: Fuel up in Wawa or White River — the White River-to-Marathon leg is long with few services.
Agawa Rock Pictographs closes in high wind/wave — check conditions before the short exposed trail.
Book Hattie Cove (Pukaskwa) ahead in shoulder season; it's the park's only frontcountry campground.

safety.cellCoverage: Long dead zones between Sault Ste. Marie and Thunder Bay — tell someone your plan.
safety.note: This is bear country — standard food storage discipline at all campsites.

pois.name: Petro-Canada (Great Northern Rd)
pois.note: Large fuel stop on the main commercial strip entering Sault Ste. Marie from the east.

pois.name: Circle K / Esso (Hwy 17 & Hwy 101 Junction)
pois.note: Fuel and snacks at the junction where Hwy 101 to Chapleau meets Hwy 17 in Wawa.

pois.name: Albert's & Son's Husky
pois.note: Long-standing Husky truck stop on Hwy 17, a key fuel stop in remote White River.

pois.name: Petro-Canada Marathon
pois.note: Roadside fuel stop on Hwy 17 as it passes Marathon, before the long stretch to Nipigon.

pois.name: Husky Travel Centre
pois.note: Full-service truck stop with diesel, showers and restaurant at the Hwy 17/11 split.

pois.name: Voyageurs' Lodge & Cookhouse
pois.note: Popular lakeside restaurant and lodge right on Hwy 17, known for hearty comfort food.
pois.nearTown: Batchawana Bay, ON (near Sault Ste. Marie)

pois.name: Kinniwabi Pines Restaurant
pois.note: Long-running family restaurant on Hwy 17 just south of Wawa, a classic road-trip stop.

pois.name: A&W White River
pois.note: Reliable quick-service burger stop on Hwy 17 in the self-proclaimed 'coldest spot in Canada'.

pois.name: Rossport Inn
pois.note: Historic inn and dining room in the scenic fishing village of Rossport, just off Hwy 17.

pois.name: Hoito Restaurant
pois.note: Iconic century-old Finnish restaurant in Thunder Bay, famous for all-day pancake breakfasts.

pois.name: Hattie Cove Campground
pois.note: Pukaskwa National Park's only frontcountry campground, with RV sites and Lake Superior access.

pois.name: Agawa Bay Campground
pois.note: Large sandy-beach campground in Lake Superior Provincial Park, RV-friendly with a scenic shoreline.

pois.name: Rabbit Blanket Lake Campground
pois.note: Quieter inland campground near the north end of Lake Superior Provincial Park, close to Wawa.

pois.name: Neys Provincial Park Campground
pois.note: Scenic Lake Superior beachfront campground with RV sites, west of Marathon on Hwy 17.

pois.name: Rainbow Falls Provincial Park Campground
pois.note: Two-campground park on Whitesand Lake near Rossport, a good overnight stop before Thunder Bay.

pois.name: Wawa Goose
pois.note: The giant roadside Canada goose statue, an essential photo-op landmark at Wawa's welcome centre.

pois.name: Agawa Rock Pictographs
pois.note: Short but exposed trail to Ojibwe rock paintings on a cliff face above Lake Superior; caution in wind/waves.

pois.name: Old Woman Bay
pois.note: Sweeping sand-and-rock beach beneath tall cliffs, one of the most photographed views on Hwy 17.

pois.name: Southern Headland / Coastal Hiking Trail
pois.note: Easy loop trail from Hattie Cove over rocky headlands with classic Pukaskwa coastline views.

pois.name: Terry Fox Memorial and Lookout
pois.note: Statue and viewpoint overlooking Lake Superior and the Sleeping Giant, marking Fox's Marathon of Hope.

pois.name: Kakabeka Falls
pois.note: Dramatic 40 m waterfall on the Kaministiquia River with boardwalk viewing platforms, west of Thunder Bay.

zones.label: Boundary Waters, Quetico & Kenora
zones.blurb: Canadian Shield lake country — Quetico's canoe-country quiet gives way to Kenora's Lake of the Woods waterfront.
tips: Quetico is a wilderness park — Dawson Trail is the only real drive-in campground.
Kenora's harbourfront (Husky the Muskie) is an easy stretch-the-legs stop with parking for larger rigs.

safety.cellCoverage: Reliable in Atikokan and Kenora; gaps in Quetico's interior.

pois.name: Johnson's Esso
pois.note: Esso fuel stop in Atikokan on Hwy 11B, handy last fill-up before heading into Quetico.

pois.name: Husky Travel Centre
pois.note: Husky station/truck stop on Hwy 17 E in Kenora with easy big-rig and RV access.

pois.name: Red River Co-op Gas Bar
pois.note: Local co-op gas bar along the Hwy 17 corridor through Kenora.

pois.name: Voyageur Bait and Tackle
pois.note: Combined fuel and bait/tackle shop on Hwy 11B in Atikokan, useful trip-planning stop.

pois.name: The Grill at Little Falls
pois.note: Popular local diner-style eatery near Little Falls on the edge of Atikokan.

pois.name: Sapawe Corner Diner
pois.note: Classic highway diner on Hwy 623, a short detour north of Atikokan off Hwy 11.

pois.name: Waterside Restaurant (Lakeside Inn)
pois.note: Sit-down dining at the Lakeside Inn overlooking Lake of the Woods in downtown Kenora.

pois.name: Boathouse Lakeside Grill
pois.note: Waterfront eatery and patio right on the Kenora harbourfront.

pois.name: Dawson Trail Campground (Quetico PP)
pois.note: Quetico's main drive-in campground at French Lake off Hwy 11, sites suit trailers/campervans.

pois.name: Anicinabe Park Campground
pois.note: City-run campground and RV park on Lake of the Woods within Kenora, full hookups available.

pois.name: Rushing River Provincial Park
pois.note: Popular provincial park east of Kenora on Hwy 17 with RV-friendly sites near a swimming falls.

pois.name: Pye's Landing
pois.note: Lake of the Woods resort/campground in Clearwater Bay, north of Kenora via Hwy 658.

pois.name: Husky the Muskie
pois.note: Giant fibreglass muskie statue at McLeod Park, an iconic Kenora waterfront photo stop.

pois.name: Kenora Harbourfront / McLeod Park
pois.note: Waterfront park and boardwalk on Lake of the Woods, good spot to stretch legs and take photos.

pois.name: Pickerel Point Trail (Quetico PP)
pois.note: Short, easy interpretive trail near the French Lake park office in Quetico Provincial Park.

pois.name: Rushing River Lower Falls Trail
pois.note: Short trail to a scenic waterfall on the Rushing River, just off Hwy 17 east of Kenora.

zones.label: Manitoba Prairies & Riding Mountain
zones.blurb: Winnipeg's Forks for a city break, then north into Riding Mountain's forested escarpment and its free-roaming bison herd.
tips: The Forks Market is the easiest one-stop lunch for a big group.
Lake Audy's bison enclosure is a drive-through — best light early morning or late afternoon.
Wasagaming Campground has full hookups; book ahead for September weekends.

safety.cellCoverage: Good in Winnipeg and Wasagaming townsite; spottier in the park's backcountry (Grey Owl's Cabin trail).
safety.nearestHospital: Winnipeg or McCreary/Onanole near the park
safety.note: Standard 911 coverage on Hwy 1 and Hwy 10.

pois.name: Petro-Pass Truck Stop (Petro-Canada)
pois.note: Big rig-friendly truck stop at Hwy 1 & Hwy 16 junction, Portage la Prairie.

pois.name: Petro-Canada - 1284 Portage Avenue
pois.note: Convenient fuel stop on Portage Ave heading west out of downtown Winnipeg.

pois.name: Co-op Gas Bar - 3755 Portage Avenue
pois.note: Co-op fuel bar on west Portage Ave, last easy fill-up before leaving the city.

pois.name: Petro-Canada - Minnedosa (Hwy 1 & Hwy 10)
pois.note: Fuel stop at the Trans-Canada/Hwy 10 junction, the turnoff north toward Riding Mountain.

pois.name: Tall Grass Prairie Bread Co. & Deli
pois.note: Organic bakery/deli inside The Forks Market, good sandwiches and fresh bread for the road.

pois.name: SMITH Restaurant
pois.note: Sit-down restaurant at the Inn at the Forks with river-view patio seating.

pois.name: The Forks Market
pois.note: Historic market hall with dozens of food vendors, an easy one-stop lunch break.

pois.name: Whitehouse Bakery & Restaurant
pois.note: Wasagaming institution famous for cinnamon buns; hearty breakfasts and baked goods.

pois.name: Lakehouse Restaurant
pois.note: Clear Lake dining with lake views, casual to upscale Canadian fare.

pois.name: Wasagaming Campground
pois.note: Large Parks Canada campground in the townsite with full RV hookups and Clear Lake access.

pois.name: Moon Lake Campground
pois.note: Quieter Parks Canada campground a short drive from Wasagaming, treed sites for tents/small RVs.

pois.name: Whirlpool Lake Campground
pois.note: Backcountry-feel drive-in campground deeper in the park, more remote and rustic.

pois.name: Clear Lake Golf Course RV overflow area
pois.note: Overflow camping area near the golf course used during peak Wasagaming demand.

pois.name: Grey Owl's Cabin Trail (Ajawaan Lake)
pois.note: Long trail to naturalist Grey Owl's historic cabin site on Ajawaan Lake; a full-day hike.

pois.name: Bald Hill & Gorge Creek Trail
pois.note: Loop trail with escarpment views over the prairie, popular moderate day hike.

pois.name: Lake Audy Bison Enclosure
pois.note: Drive-through enclosure where a plains bison herd roams; good wildlife photo stop.

pois.name: Clear Lake
pois.note: Central lake of the park with a sandy beach boardwalk right in the Wasagaming townsite.

pois.name: The Forks Riverwalk
pois.note: Paved riverside path at the confluence of the Red and Assiniboine Rivers in downtown Winnipeg.

zones.label: Saskatchewan & Alberta Prairies
zones.blurb: Big-sky prairie driving through Regina, Moose Jaw's tunnels and murals, and Medicine Hat's river valley.
tips: Moose Jaw's Tunnels tour is worth booking ahead in peak season.
Red Rock Coulee is a ~45 min detour south of Medicine Hat — worth it for the sandstone formations.
Long flat stretches here are the best place to bank extra fuel-range margin.

safety.cellCoverage: Strong throughout — this is the most connected stretch of the whole route.
safety.nearestHospital: Regina, Moose Jaw, or Medicine Hat
safety.note: Standard 911 coverage; watch for sudden prairie thunderstorms in shoulder season.

pois.name: Husky Travel Centre
pois.note: Big truck stop on TCH East edge of Regina; diesel, restaurant, easy big-rig/RV access.

pois.name: Petro-Canada (Victoria Ave)
pois.note: Major chain station on Victoria Ave, the TCH corridor through east Regina.

pois.name: Co-op Gas Bar
pois.note: Federated Co-op fuel stop at 414 9th Ave SW, just off the highway in Moose Jaw.

pois.name: Flying J Travel Center
pois.note: Full truck stop at 2194 Saamis Dr NW; showers, diesel lanes, good RV turnaround.

pois.name: Trans-Canada Husky (Husky House)
pois.note: Long-standing Husky/Esso stop at 561 15 St SW along the TCH in Medicine Hat.

pois.name: Bushwakker Brewpub
pois.note: Regina's original craft brewpub, 2206 Dewdney Ave; hearty pub fare and house beer.

pois.name: The Diplomat Steakhouse
pois.note: Long-running upscale steakhouse at 2032 Broad St, a Regina dinner institution since 1963.

pois.name: Houston Pizza
pois.note: Original location, 117 Main St N; homegrown Saskatchewan pizza chain founded in Moose Jaw.

pois.name: Sabai Infusion
pois.note: Popular Thai restaurant at 638 2nd St SE in downtown Medicine Hat.

pois.name: Eat's on 8th
pois.note: Casual homemade-food takeout/eatery at 13 8 St NW, downtown Medicine Hat.

pois.name: #1 RV Campground
pois.note: RV park and storage on the east side of Regina near the TCH, geared to travelers.

pois.name: Buffalo Pound Provincial Park
pois.note: Lakeside provincial park with campgrounds ~25 min north of Moose Jaw off Hwy 2/301.

pois.name: Moose Jaw KOA Journey
pois.note: KOA-brand campground with full RV hookups just outside Moose Jaw.

pois.name: Gas City Campground
pois.note: City-run campground at 402 11 Ave SW, close to downtown Medicine Hat and the river.

pois.name: Ross Creek RV Park
pois.note: RV park east of Medicine Hat off the TCH, popular overnight stop for road-trippers.

pois.name: Wascana Centre
pois.note: Huge urban park around Wascana Lake with the Legislature, paths, and waterfowl.

pois.name: Tunnels of Moose Jaw
pois.note: Guided historic tunnel tours (bootlegging/immigrant history) at 18 Main St N.

pois.name: Murals of Moose Jaw
pois.note: Dozens of large outdoor historical murals painted across downtown building walls.

pois.name: Police Point Park
pois.note: Riverside natural park with trails and boardwalks along the South Saskatchewan River.

pois.name: Red Rock Coulee Natural Area
pois.note: Giant reddish sandstone concretions/hoodoo-like formations, ~45 min south of Medicine Hat.

zones.label: Calgary & Canadian Rockies Front Range
zones.blurb: The postcard stretch — Banff, Lake Louise, Moraine Lake, and Yoho's waterfalls, all within a couple hours of Calgary.
tips: Moraine Lake and Lake Louise often require a shuttle/reservation in peak season — check Parks Canada ahead.
Banff/Yoho campgrounds book out fast; reserve well ahead for Sept weekends.
This is the most tourist-dense zone on the route — arrive at trailheads early.

safety.cellCoverage: Good in Banff/Canmore townsites; drops off along the Icefields Parkway and in Yoho's backcountry.
safety.nearestHospital: Banff Mineral Springs Hospital or Canmore General
safety.note: Wildlife country — bear spray recommended on any trail here.

pois.name: Petro-Canada Banff
pois.note: Central gas station on Lynx St in Banff townsite, easy access for RVs.

pois.name: Petro-Canada Canmore (Bow Valley Trail)
pois.note: Well-known fuel stop on Bow Valley Trail before heading into the mountains.

pois.name: Shell Bow Valley Trail Canmore
pois.note: Alternate Canmore fuel stop with convenience store, good last-fill before Banff NP.

pois.name: Husky Travel Centre Calgary (Trans-Canada Hwy)
pois.note: Truck-stop-style station on the eastern Trans-Canada approach into Calgary, diesel and RV-friendly pumps.

pois.name: Costco Gas Calgary NW (Sarcee Trail)
pois.note: Discount fuel near Trans-Canada/Sarcee Trail interchange; membership required.

pois.name: Petro-Pass Truck Stop Medicine Hat
pois.note: Truck-stop fuel and services on the Trans-Canada corridor through Medicine Hat.

pois.name: Eddie Burger + Bar
pois.note: Popular casual burger joint on Banff Avenue, local favorite for a quick hearty meal.

pois.name: The Bison Restaurant
pois.note: Upscale Alberta-sourced dining on Bear Street with a rooftop patio.

pois.name: Wild Flour Bakery
pois.note: Organic bakery/cafe on Bear Street, good for pastries and coffee before a hike.

pois.name: communitea Cafe
pois.note: Laid-back Canmore cafe known for healthy bowls, wraps, and tea.

pois.name: Le Fournil Bakery
pois.note: French-style bakery in Canmore for croissants and bread, good early-morning stop.

pois.name: River Cafe
pois.note: Destination restaurant on Prince's Island Park in downtown Calgary, seasonal Canadian menu.

pois.name: Tunnel Mountain Village I Campground
pois.note: Large Parks Canada campground near Banff townsite with powered RV sites.

pois.name: Tunnel Mountain Village II Campground
pois.note: Year-round Parks Canada campground, popular RV base close to downtown Banff.

pois.name: Two Jack Lakeside Campground
pois.note: Scenic lakeside Parks Canada campground east of Banff townsite, RV and tent sites.

pois.name: Bow River Campground (Bow Valley Provincial Park)
pois.note: Alberta Parks campground along the Bow River between Calgary and Canmore, RV-friendly.

pois.name: Kicking Horse Campground
pois.note: Parks Canada campground in Yoho National Park near Field, BC, suitable for RVs.

pois.name: Lake Louise Campground (Trailer/RV Loop)
pois.note: Parks Canada campground in Lake Louise village with a fenced RV/trailer loop.

pois.name: Grassi Lakes
pois.note: Short scenic hike to turquoise twin lakes just outside Canmore.

pois.name: Spray Lakes Reservoir
pois.note: Long turquoise reservoir with pullouts and viewpoints on Smith-Dorrien Trail near Canmore.

pois.name: Lake Louise
pois.note: Iconic glacial lake with Chateau Lake Louise backdrop, extremely popular photo stop.

pois.name: Moraine Lake
pois.note: Valley of the Ten Peaks backdrop; access often requires shuttle/parking reservation in peak season.

pois.name: Johnston Canyon
pois.note: Catwalk trail along a canyon to lower and upper waterfalls, on the Bow Valley Parkway.

pois.name: Emerald Lake
pois.note: Vividly colored lake with lakeshore trail and lodge, in Yoho National Park.

pois.name: Takakkaw Falls
pois.note: One of Canada's tallest waterfalls, short walk from the Yoho Valley Road parking lot.

pois.name: Banff Gondola (Sulphur Mountain)
pois.note: Gondola to a summit boardwalk with panoramic views over Banff and the Bow Valley.

zones.label: Columbia Mountains & Okanagan
zones.blurb: Rogers Pass's avalanche country and Mount Revelstoke's alpine parkway, descending into the Shuswap and Okanagan's lake valleys.
tips: Rogers Pass can see early snow by late September — check DriveBC before crossing.
Meadows in the Sky Parkway (Revelstoke) is closed to trailers/large RVs — check current vehicle limits.
Splatsin Centre near Enderby is the trip's home base for the final days — Riverside RV Park is the closest full-hookup option.

safety.cellCoverage: Gaps through Rogers Pass and Glacier NP; solid again by Revelstoke.
safety.note: Mountain pass driving — check DriveBC.ca for Rogers Pass conditions before departing Golden.

pois.name: Husky Travel Centre
pois.note: Truck-stop-style fuel and diesel on the Trans-Canada in Golden, easy big-rig/RV access.

pois.name: Petro-Canada (9th Ave N)
pois.note: In-town Golden fuel stop with convenience store, close to downtown.

pois.name: Petro-Canada (Trans-Canada Hwy)
pois.note: Highway-side fuel stop on the west approach to Revelstoke.

pois.name: Petro-Canada (Trans-Canada Hwy)
pois.note: Convenient highway fuel stop on the Trans-Canada through Salmon Arm.

pois.name: Gen7 Fuel (Quilakwa)
pois.note: Indigenous-owned gas bar on Hwy 97A between Vernon and Enderby.

pois.name: The Wolf's Den Restaurant
pois.note: Casual pub-style steaks, burgers and local beer near Kicking Horse in Golden.

pois.name: Bacchus Books & Cafe
pois.note: Bookstore cafe on 9th Ave N serving coffee and light meals in a cozy setting.

pois.name: The Modern Bakeshop & Cafe
pois.note: Revelstoke's most popular bakery-cafe on Mackenzie Ave, great pastries and lunch.

pois.name: Conversations Coffee House
pois.note: Long-running downtown Revelstoke coffee shop, good for a work-and-coffee break.

pois.name: Salmon Arm Farmers' Market
pois.note: Seasonal downtown market for local produce, baked goods and snacks (Saturdays).

pois.name: Bean Scene Coffee House
pois.note: Historic downtown Vernon coffeehouse, popular local hangout with patio seating.

pois.name: Illecillewaet Campground
pois.note: Parks Canada frontcountry campground at Rogers Pass, RV-friendly, no hookups.

pois.name: Blanket Creek Provincial Park
pois.note: Riverside BC Parks campground south of Revelstoke with swimming hole and waterfall trail.

pois.name: Martha Creek Provincial Park
pois.note: Quiet BC Parks campground on Upper Arrow Lake north of Revelstoke, RV sites available.

pois.name: Herald Provincial Park
pois.note: Shuswap Lake BC Parks campground near Tappen with sandy beach, good RV sites.

pois.name: Riverside RV Park and Campground
pois.note: Full-hookup RV park on the Shuswap River right in Enderby, popular base for the Okanagan leg.

pois.name: Rogers Pass Summit
pois.note: Summit viewpoint and Discovery Centre at 1,330m, avalanche-history exhibits and photo stop.

pois.name: Meeting of the Waters Trail
pois.note: Short easy trail where the Asulkan and Illecillewaet creeks converge, great glacier-fed water views.

pois.name: Meadows in the Sky Parkway
pois.note: 26 km scenic drive up Mount Revelstoke to alpine meadows and a 360-degree summit viewpoint.

pois.name: Enderby Cliffs (Tplaqin) Trail
pois.note: Steep but rewarding hike to dramatic cliff-edge viewpoints over the Shuswap River valley.

pois.name: Salmon Arm Wharf & Marine Park
pois.note: Canada's longest curved wooden wharf, easy lakeside walk and prime birdwatching spot.

pois.name: Kalamalka Lake Provincial Park
pois.note: Cosens Bay/Kal Beach viewpoints over the famously turquoise 'Lake of Many Colours'.

zones.label: Icefields Parkway & Thompson Country
zones.blurb: Used by the alternate 10-day route only — the Icefields Parkway's glaciers, Mount Robson, and Wells Gray's waterfalls on the way to Kelowna.
tips: Fuel up in Jasper — there are no services on the Icefields Parkway itself between Jasper and Lake Louise.
Athabasca & Sunwapta Falls are both roadside-easy; Columbia Icefield's toe-of-the-glacier walk needs sturdy shoes.
Helmcken Falls (Wells Gray) is a short walk from parking — worth the detour up Clearwater Valley Rd.

safety.cellCoverage: Very little coverage on the Icefields Parkway itself — download offline maps and tell someone your route.
safety.note: Wildlife on the Parkway at dawn/dusk — reduce speed.

pois.name: Petro-Canada Jasper
pois.note: Fuel stop in Jasper townsite on Connaught Dr, walkable to shops and the train station.

pois.name: Petro-Canada Clearwater
pois.note: Last major fuel stop before heading up Clearwater Valley Rd into Wells Gray Park.

pois.name: Kamloops Travel Centre (Petro-Pass Truck Stop)
pois.note: Full-service truck stop on the Trans-Canada Hwy with diesel, RV-friendly pumps and a diner.

pois.name: Petro-Canada Harvey Ave
pois.note: Convenient fuel stop on Hwy 97 (Harvey Ave) through central Kelowna.

pois.name: Bear's Paw Bakery
pois.note: Beloved Jasper bakery for morning pastries, sourdough and strong coffee before hitting the parkway.

pois.name: Jasper Pizza Place
pois.note: Long-running downtown Jasper pizzeria with wood-fired pies, popular with hikers.

pois.name: Helmcken Falls Lodge Restaurant
pois.note: Rustic lodge dining room on Clearwater Valley Rd near the Wells Gray park entrance.

pois.name: The Noble Pig Brewhouse
pois.note: Downtown Kamloops craft brewpub with hearty pub fare and local beer.

pois.name: Bliss Bakery & Bistro
pois.note: Popular Bernard Ave bakery-cafe in downtown Kelowna for baked goods and brunch.

pois.name: RauDZ Regional Table
pois.note: Well-regarded Kelowna restaurant near the waterfront focused on Okanagan-sourced ingredients.

pois.name: Wapiti Campground
pois.note: Large Parks Canada campground just south of Jasper townsite, some sites open year-round.

pois.name: Whistlers Campground
pois.note: Jasper's biggest campground near the Jasper SkyTram, with serviced RV sites.

pois.name: Wabasso Campground
pois.note: Quieter Parks Canada campground on Hwy 93A near Mount Edith Cavell Rd.

pois.name: Columbia Icefield Campground
pois.note: Basic tent/small-RV campground on the Icefields Parkway just north of the Icefield Centre.

pois.name: Clearwater Lake Campground
pois.note: BC Parks campground at the north end of Clearwater Valley Rd inside Wells Gray Park.

pois.name: Okanagan Lake Provincial Park Campground
pois.note: Lakeside BC Parks campground north of Kelowna near Okanagan Centre, sandy swimming beach.

pois.name: Columbia Icefield / Athabasca Glacier
pois.note: Iconic glacier viewpoint on the Icefields Parkway; Ice Explorer tours and short glacier-toe hike.

pois.name: Peyto Lake Viewpoint
pois.note: Short trail to a famous overlook of the turquoise, wolf-head-shaped Peyto Lake.

pois.name: Sunwapta Falls
pois.note: Powerful canyon waterfall right off the Icefields Parkway, easy short walk from parking.

pois.name: Athabasca Falls
pois.note: Narrow, thunderous falls through quartzite canyon; one of the most-visited stops on the parkway.

pois.name: Mount Robson Viewpoint
